newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash soymeal-Offers mostly flat, selling slow.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash soymeal-Offers mostly flat, selling slow.

text.p: U.S. rail and truck soymeal basis offers were mostly steady on Thursday and demand was light as end-users continued to buy hand to mouth, several brokers said.
"There's really not a whole lot of domestic demand," a Tennessee broker said. "They're waiting to see when harvest puts pressure on the basis numbers."

Brokers noted a slightly weaker tone in parts of Illinois and Alabama tied to weak demand. Offers dropped $2.00 in Chicago but held steady elsewhere. Offers firmed $1.00 in Kansas City after falling $2.00 on Wednesday.

Brokers also noted CBOT September soymeal futures were trading at about a $10 per ton premium to the October. They said many end-users were not interested in buying until the September contract expired later this month.
There were scattered reports of processors in Minnesota and Indiana taking downtime this week.
